subject: Testing interfaces on changes to the Stan project

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Testing interfaces on changes to the Stan project
parts:
From Marcus:

Can we just run the unit tests of stan instead of cmdstan for tests that only touch stan? We don't run rstan or pystan unit tests for each merge we do to stan right now. Ideally we should in order to catch when wrappers break, but that's another issue...

Anyway, my understanding of git submodules is that they link to a specific revision which is itself version controlled. That means in order to update stan within cmdstan someone needs to submit a PR with a change to the linked version. Maybe the process should then become: 1) do development on stan then 2) once PRs are tested/merged in stan, submit a PR to cmdstan to update the submodule to the new point on develop which would be separately unit tested. This will make things somewhat tedious to develop though. It's also somewhat error prone because cmdstan and stan could then fall out of sync.

messages.subject: Re: Testing interfaces on changes to the Stan project
parts:
On Sunday, May 4, 2014 5:42:39 PM UTC-4, Daniel Lee wrote:

From Marcus:

Can we just run the unit tests of stan instead of cmdstan for tests that only touch stan? We don't run rstan or pystan unit tests for each merge we do to stan right now. Ideally we should in order to catch when wrappers break, but that's another issue...

That's where we're going with the relationship between Stan and its interfaces. Right now, we've (almost) got the system set up for CmdStan. After the refactoring effort I'm going through, we'll have RStan going too.
Anyway, my understanding of git submodules is that they link to a specific revision which is itself version controlled.
That is true, but it works slightly differently than that. For the development branch of CmdStan, we are going to be compatible to the current version of Stan.
That means in order to update stan within cmdstan someone needs to submit a PR with a change to the linked version.
That is false. The minimum number of pull requests needed is 1: one per tagged version of Stan.

Maybe the process should then become: 1) do development on stan then 2) once PRs are tested/merged in stan, submit a PR to cmdstan to update the submodule to the new point on develop which would be separately unit tested. This will make things somewhat tedious to develop though. It's also somewhat error prone because cmdstan and stan could then fall out of sync.

Exactly. So the way it works now is, work on Stan, commit, submit a pull request. If you're working on core Stan, you won't be affecting the interfaces; we'll test through the interface(s) just to make sure things are compatible. (We have this issue now where the pull request made on Stan doesn't propagate through the CmdStan's submodule of Stan, but hopefully we can fix that... the temporary fix is to create a branch on Stan that has the changes and the pull requests will go through).

If the pull request actually stops CmdStan, RStan, or *Stan from building, that should not go into Stan as-is. I'm going to be adamant about that. The last thing we want is for developers not to trust the current state of any of the interfaces because it's out of synch.




Daniel
